whyItMatters: CodeBuild can execute code with high-value credentials, environment variables, and artifact access. Baseline visibility into build launches is essential for detecting build-path abuse.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may trigger builds to execute under a privileged build role, access secrets, or stage malicious changes in CI/CD workflows.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive because build systems often have broad permissions and trusted network access.
threatContext.whyItMatters: StartBuild is the feeder event for higher-confidence detections involving overrides, unexpected actors, and post-build sensitive activity.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may not notice the beginning of CodeBuild-based credential theft or CI/CD abuse.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for CodeBuild
loggingRequirements: CloudTrail must ingest CodeBuild management events.
The platform should preserve project name and any request overrides.
Follow-on IAM, STS, Secrets Manager, and KMS activity should be available for downstream correlation.
limitations: A single StartBuild event is usually low-context by itself.
High-volume CI/CD environments may produce a steady stream of expected build launches.
The baseline does not prove whether the launched build was malicious.

enrichment.description: Classify the build project by privilege, secret exposure, and production impact.
Determine whether the actor is expected to start that build project.
Track whether buildspec or environment overrides were included in the request.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Helps separate ordinary builds from higher-risk launches.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This should remain a broad visibility rule for successful `StartBuild` events. It provides the baseline execution telemetry required for more targeted CodeBuild abuse detections.
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Keep the baseline broad. 2. Add project criticality and actor context for triage. 3. Correlate with overrides or later sensitive activity for higher-confidence detections.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire on every successful StartBuild event for visibility.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Medium as a baseline visibility rule, low-medium with actor and project context

deployment.scheduling: Real-time is useful for chaining into override and post-build abuse detections.
considerations: This is the feeder rule for the CodeBuild credential-theft family.
Project criticality and actor context are the main enrichments.
